summary: Run 3 of M1-S03, a targeted rebuild after the operator's dry-run validation 3 compiled run 2's package and returned eleven errors - two roots and nine cascade. Exactly two faults were fixed, in three call sites across three files, and every other file is byte-identical to run 2. Root 1: URL.getSalesforceBaseUrl() was removed after version 58.0 and these classes are pinned to 67.0, so both call sites now use URL.getOrgDomainUrl().toExternalForm(). Root 2: IntegrationFailureResendTest filtered SOQL on Request_Payload__c, a Long Text Area the platform will not filter, group or sort, so the two WHERE clauses were replaced by one select-then-pick helper pair that asserts on the selected value. The nine cascade errors needed no edit. All three declared checkers exit 0 with zero findings, check-outputs is ok on all 20 declared paths, every meta XML parses at 67.0, and brace/paren/bracket/string balance holds across all 12 Apex files. Run 3 has not been compiled by any org.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per GATES.md Gate D row 3: Gate B resolves every symbol and Gate C's compile check did not run, because build_mode is design-only and there is no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI. Read this MEDIUM as 'not compiled', not as 'probably fine' - run 2 carried the same computed MEDIUM on the same evidence and the org rejected it eleven times. The two known defects are fixed against the org's own verbatim messages rather than against a guess, which is the only reason this is not LOW; what would raise it is a green dry run 4, which no agent in this loop may perform.

findings.title: An attested identifier shipped and did not compile: attestation is not a version gate
findings.detail: Run 2 emitted URL.getSalesforceBaseUrl().toExternalForm() in two classes. The org answered 'Method was removed after version 58.0: getSalesforceBaseUrl' and these classes are pinned to 67.0. The name passed Gate C check 2 legitimately: three skills in this repo spell it, so the grep that backs identifier provenance returned a hit. What none of those three carries is the version gate. A repo grep answers 'does the corpus spell this name', and the question that decides whether a package deploys is 'is this name legal at the apiVersion this step stamps into its meta XML'. Nothing offline caught the gap - not the three checkers, not the XML parse, not the brace scan. Only the org did.

evidence.attested_in: three skills under skills/ spell getSalesforceBaseUrl; none names a version ceiling

findings.recommendation: Fixed in this run: both call sites use URL.getOrgDomainUrl().toExternalForm(), the form the Apex Developer Guide's examples use at this version (apexdev L32630, L37043). The three skills carrying the removed method are a library defect the operator has already logged as S2-F-04; they are not this step's to edit. The durable fix for the agent is that Gate C check 2 should ask for a version, not only for a hit.

findings.title: A SOQL filter on a Long Text Area, which the platform will not run
findings.detail: IntegrationFailureResendTest selected its two fixture rows with WHERE Request_Payload__c != NULL and WHERE Request_Payload__c = NULL. M1-S01 declares that field <type>LongTextArea</type>, and long and rich text areas cannot be filtered, grouped or sorted. No checker in this step's declared set reads SOQL against the field types another step wrote, so nothing offline could have seen it.

findings.title: The org loses its trigger kill switch and its data-load bypass (still open)

Remedy B dropped templates/apex/TriggerHandler.cls because its closure needs TriggerControl and Trigger_Setting__mdt, which no step ships. A bulk load that reassigns Case ownership into Tier_2_Engineering will escalate every affected Case with no bypass, and switching the feature off is a deployment of CaseTrigger.trigger-meta.xml with status Inactive.

findings.title: Tier2_Escalation__e.Severity__c is mapped from Case.Priority and nothing says it should be (still open)
findings.detail: Unchanged from run 2. No clarification maps the event's Severity__c to a Case field; Priority is the only severity-shaped field this build has seen. Q11's answer speaks of 'a Severity 1 escalation', which is not the shape of standard Case.Priority values. An inline // UNVERIFIED comment sits on the assignment itself. A wrong value here is silently wrong on the dashboard - the compiler cannot see it and neither can any checker.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the ops dashboard team before UAT. Dry run 4 will not surface it.

process_observations.observation: Nine of the eleven org errors were cascade - Dependent class is invalid on five classes and Variable does not exist on both triggers - and every one of them cleared by fixing its root, so the rebuild touched three call sites rather than the eight components the error list named.
M1-S04's four classes compiled clean in the same request, so the two faults are specific to this step's code rather than to the build's shared assumptions about API version or the object model.

Every offline gate this step has - three declared checkers at zero findings, an XML parse, a brace and string-balance scan, and an identifier grep over the whole corpus - passed on a package the org rejected eleven times; the two faults were a version-gated method and a field-type constraint, and no offline artefact in this repo encodes either fact about this build's own metadata.

The identifier-provenance check this agent runs asks whether the corpus spells a name and cannot ask whether the name is legal at the apiVersion the step stamps into its own meta XML - which is exactly the gap that shipped getSalesforceBaseUrl into a 67.0 class, from three skills that spell it without naming a ceiling.
